stages.title: TERMINOLOGY, CHRONOLOGY AND THE INTEGRATION-LOCALISATION MODEL — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Terminology, Chronology And The Integration-Localisation Model — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Terminology to Chronology, then testing the relationship through The Integration-Localisation Model and Early Harappan.
stages.mechanism: The tripartite scheme describes processes, not three sealed ethnic populations.
stages.consequence: Protohistory here means a literate civilization whose script cannot yet be read.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: mature Harappan and Rig Vedic are contemporaneous. || Mature Harappan urbanism largely predates the...
stages.answer: "Harappan" is the safest archaeological label because the culture extended far beyond the Indus valley and the identification of the Ghaggar-Hakra with the Vedic Sarasvati remains debated.

stages.title: DISCOVERY, EXCAVATION AND CHANGING HISTORIOGRAPHY
stages.terms: Technically, Discovery, Excavation And Changing Historiography is analysed by relating Discovery to Excavation, then testing the relationship through Changing Historiography and Marshall.
stages.mechanism: Research moved from spectacular citadels and artefacts toward households, villages, plant and animal remains, human biology, provenance and environmental histories.
stages.consequence: New methods have not removed interpretation; they have made the evidentiary chain more explicit.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: the first excavator's label proves a structure's function. || Labels must be retested against...
stages.answer: Historiography is a movement from diffusion, monarchy and invasion toward indigenous development, regional variation and multidisciplinary process.

stages.title: GEOGRAPHICAL EXTENT, ECOLOGICAL ZONES AND REGIONAL DOMAINS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Geographical Extent, Ecological Zones And Regional Domains — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Geographical Extent to Ecological Zones, then testing the relationship through Regional Domains and Indus alluvium.
stages.mechanism: Use "vast, multi-ecological zone" rather than one immutable number.
stages.consequence: Shortughai in Afghanistan was an isolated trading outpost.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: indus Valley Civilization means all sites lie in the Indus valley. || The distribution...
stages.answer: Ecological diversity explains both civilizational resilience and regionally varied pathways of decline.

stages.title: FROM EARLIER FARMING COMMUNITIES TO EARLY HARAPPAN URBAN POTENTIAL
stages.terms: Technically, From Earlier Farming Communities To Early Harappan Urban Potential is analysed by relating Kot Diji to Fortification, citadel-lower area, wheel-made pottery and copper, then testing the relationship through Planning and hierarchy preceded mature cities and Rehman Dheri.
stages.mechanism: Explain origins as endogenous transformation with inter-regional interaction, not a Mesopotamian colony or one-site diffusion.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that explain origins as endogenous transformation with inter-regional interaction, not a Mesopotamian colony or one-site...
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: early Harappan means primitive and unplanned. || Several early settlements were fortified, planned and...
stages.answer: Urbanisation emerged through convergence among regional traditions, craft intensification, exchange, agricultural surplus, leadership and ideology; no single trigger is sufficient.

stages.title: SETTLEMENT HIERARCHY AND THE URBAN-RURAL SYSTEM — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: The civilization was urban, but most settlements were villages.
stages.mechanism: The civilization was urban, but most settlements were villages.
stages.consequence: Allahdino was a small village with precious ornaments, showing that wealth was not confined to great cities.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: urban civilization means every Harappan settlement was a city. || The settlement network was...
stages.answer: Standardisation across this hierarchy required coordination, but it does not by itself prove one centralized empire.

stages.title: SITE ATLAS I - HARAPPA AND MOHENJO-DARO — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Pair the two sites to show shared standards plus different public landscapes.
stages.mechanism: Mohenjo-daro may have had over 700 wells, including private and neighbourhood wells.
stages.consequence: Its secure significance is collective engineering; ritual bathing is plausible, not proven.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: the Great Bath proves a named religion. || It proves sophisticated waterproof public architecture.
stages.answer: Pair the two sites to show shared standards plus different public landscapes.

stages.title: SITE ATLAS II - DHOLAVIRA AND RAKHIGARHI — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Site Atlas Ii - Dholavira And Rakhigarhi — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Site Atlas Ii - Dholavira to Rakhigarhi, then testing the relationship through Dholavira and Regional adaptation, water governance and civic writing.
stages.mechanism: It demonstrates civic display of writing but does not reveal the city's name until the script is deciphered.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that dholavira supplies architecture and climate adaptation.
stages.trap: Rakhigarhi DNA settled every question of Harappan identity. || One low-coverage ancient genome was a major beginning, not a complete population history.
stages.answer: Dholavira supplies architecture and climate adaptation; Rakhigarhi supplies urban, mortuary and scientific evidence.

stages.title: SITE ATLAS III - KALIBANGAN, LOTHAL AND BANAWALI — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Site Atlas Iii - Kalibangan, Lothal And Banawali — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Site Atlas Iii - Kalibangan to Lothal, then testing the relationship through Banawali and Kalibangan.
stages.mechanism: Kalibangan's lower town lacked the Mohenjo-daro type street drains; household wastewater could empty into jars or troughs outside.
stages.consequence: This is regional variation, not urban failure.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: every fire installation proves Vedic ritual continuity. || Shape, context, chronology and associated remains...
stages.answer: Site Atlas Iii - Kalibangan, Lothal And Banawali — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] comprises Site Atlas Iii - Kalibangan, Lothal and Banawali as its core connected dimensions.

stages.title: SITE ATLAS IV - SURKOTADA, CHANHUDARO AND OTHER STRATEGIC SITES
stages.terms: Horse remains are rare and disputed; the mature civilization was not horse-centred.
stages.mechanism: Horse remains are rare and disputed; the mature civilization was not horse-centred.
stages.consequence: The humped bull and cattle economy are much more characteristic.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a reported horse bone makes the horse a defining Harappan animal. || Identification, context...
stages.answer: Chanhudaro proves that major craft production could occur in a town without the monumental form of Mohenjo-daro.

stages.title: TOWN PLANNING, ARCHITECTURE AND BUILT STANDARDS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Town Planning, Architecture And Built Standards — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Town Planning to Architecture, then testing the relationship through Built Standards and Brick standard.
stages.mechanism: Houses usually opened into side lanes and were arranged around courtyards.
stages.consequence: Baked bricks were concentrated in drains, wells, baths and important structures at many sites; mud-brick remained fundamental.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: planned layout means every city followed one blueprint. || Dholavira, Kalibangan, Lothal and smaller...
stages.answer: Town Planning, Architecture And Built Standards — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] comprises Town Planning, Architecture and Built Standards as its core connected dimensions.

stages.title: WATER, SANITATION, DRAINAGE AND COLLECTIVE MAINTENANCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Infrastructure required repeated maintenance by workers whose social position is archaeologically under-visible.
stages.mechanism: Infrastructure required repeated maintenance by workers whose social position is archaeologically under-visible.
stages.consequence: Sewage channels and rainwater collection were not necessarily the same system.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: drains prove modern public health ideas. || They prove practical sanitation and engineering.
stages.answer: Water management is a bounded contemporary bridge to urban resilience, not proof that ancient institutions were identical to modern municipalities.

stages.title: PUBLIC STRUCTURES, CRAFT ZONES AND THE PROBLEM OF FUNCTIONAL LABELS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Public buildings reveal labour mobilisation, but the responsible institution could have been rulers, councils, merchants, ritual specialists or combined authorities.
stages.mechanism: Public buildings reveal labour mobilisation, but the responsible institution could have been rulers, councils, merchants, ritual specialists or combined authorities.
stages.consequence: Use quotation marks around contested labels in Mains answers.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a large building is automatically a palace, temple or state warehouse. || Function requires...
stages.answer: Craft areas are better identified when raw material, waste, tools, unfinished pieces and furnaces occur together.

stages.title: AGRICULTURE, CROPS, SEASONS AND FOOD SURPLUS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Agriculture, Crops, Seasons And Food Surplus — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Agriculture to Crops, then testing the relationship through Seasons and Food Surplus.
stages.mechanism: Shortughai has canal evidence; Allahdino irrigation from wells is suggested but not conclusive.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that agriculture was the mainstay, but crop packages varied regionally.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: no surviving ploughshare means no ploughing. || Furrows and terracotta plough models support wooden-plough...
stages.answer: Agriculture was the mainstay, but crop packages varied regionally.

stages.title: PASTORALISM, MEAT, DAIRY, FISHING AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCE USE
stages.terms: Technically, Pastoralism, Meat, Dairy, Fishing And Environmental Resource Use is analysed by relating Pastoralism to Meat, then testing the relationship through Dairy and Fishing.
stages.mechanism: Cattle and buffalo were central; sheep, goats, pigs, dogs and cats also occur.
stages.consequence: The horse is rare, debated and not characteristic.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: an animal on a seal was necessarily domesticated or worshipped. || Representation can be...
stages.answer: Pastoralism, Meat, Dairy, Fishing And Environmental Resource Use comprises Pastoralism, Meat and Dairy as its core connected dimensions.

stages.title: CRAFT PRODUCTION, METALLURGY AND TECHNICAL SKILL — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: The bronze "Dancing Girl" was made by lost-wax casting.
stages.mechanism: The bronze "Dancing Girl" was made by lost-wax casting.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that pure copper objects were more numerous than bronze objects.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: bronze Age means every tool was bronze. || Copper, bronze, stone, shell, bone, wood...
stages.answer: Pure copper objects were more numerous than bronze objects; alloys were selected especially where harder edges were useful.

stages.title: ART AND MATERIAL CULTURE - SCULPTURE, POTTERY, TERRACOTTAS AND TOYS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Differences in materials, skill and distribution may reflect audience, function and access, not a simple high-art/low-art hierarchy.
stages.mechanism: Differences in materials, skill and distribution may reflect audience, function and access, not a simple high-art/low-art hierarchy.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that seals are among the finest artistic products.
stages.trap: A modern museum nickname is an ancient identity. || Use the nickname for recall but state its interpretive status.
stages.answer: Seals are among the finest artistic products, but terracottas range from carefully modelled to quickly made objects for everyday or short-term use.

stages.title: WEIGHTS, MEASURES, GEOMETRY AND EVIDENCE OF SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: The 2026 Prelims PYQ correctly treats weights and graduated scales as evidence of scientific knowledge, while rejecting a property-system inference from house form.
stages.mechanism: Standardization could arise through state regulation, merchant coordination, hereditary specialists, exchange networks or combinations of these.
stages.consequence: Smaller units follow a binary progression, while higher units include decimal relationships.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: "Multiple of 16" alone describes the whole weight system. || Smaller and larger series...
stages.answer: The 2026 Prelims PYQ correctly treats weights and graduated scales as evidence of scientific knowledge, while rejecting a property-system inference from house form.

stages.title: SEALS, SEALINGS AND THE UNDECIPHERED SCRIPT — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Textile impressions on some sealings support authentication of goods, but seals also show wear and suspension holes consistent with other functions.
stages.mechanism: Script non-decipherment is the master limitation governing claims about rulers, institutions and beliefs.
stages.consequence: Do not call the whole script boustrophedon.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a proposed Dravidian, Sanskrit or non-linguistic reading is settled. || Competing proposals exist.
stages.answer: Textile impressions on some sealings support authentication of goods, but seals also show wear and suspension holes consistent with other functions.

stages.title: INTERNAL EXCHANGE, RAW MATERIALS AND TRANSPORT — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Internal Exchange, Raw Materials And Transport — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Internal Exchange to Raw Materials, then testing the relationship through Transport and Copper.
stages.mechanism: Two-wheeled carts with solid wheels, pack animals, river boats and seagoing craft are supported by models, tracks and depictions.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that internal exchange was more structurally important than the visually attractive but limited Mesopotamian trade.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a non-local bead proves conquest or colony. || It proves movement.
stages.answer: Internal exchange was more structurally important than the visually attractive but limited Mesopotamian trade.

stages.title: LONG-DISTANCE TRADE, MELUHHA AND THE MESOPOTAMIAN LINK — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Possible exports include carnelian beads, textiles, shell and ivory; possible imports include selected metals and luxury materials.
stages.mechanism: Possible exports include carnelian beads, textiles, shell and ivory; possible imports include selected metals and luxury materials.
stages.consequence: Dilmun and Magan were intermediating regions, not Harappan cities.
stages.trap: Mesopotamian trade caused Harappan urbanism. || It may have enriched exchange, but chronology and low find quantities undermine a monocausal claim.
stages.answer: Dilmun is generally identified with Bahrain; Magan with Oman/Makran; Meluhha probably included the Indus region but its exact scope is debated.

stages.title: SOCIAL ORGANISATION, WEALTH AND OCCUPATIONAL DIVERSITY
stages.terms: Rank and class differences probably existed, but claims of a Harappan caste system are highly speculative.
stages.mechanism: Rank and class differences probably existed, but claims of a Harappan caste system are highly speculative.
stages.consequence: Material culture can suggest inequality more securely than it can name legal status.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: house size, location, craft access, ornaments, hoards, diet and burials indicate differentiation.
stages.answer: House size, location, craft access, ornaments, hoards, diet and burials indicate differentiation, but there are no royal tombs or lavish elite burials comparable to Egypt and Mesopotamia.

stages.title: POLITY DEBATE - EMPIRE, CITY-STATES, COUNCILS OR CORPORATE ELITES
stages.terms: Technically, Polity Debate - Empire, City-States, Councils Or Corporate Elites is analysed by relating Polity Debate - Empire to City-States, then testing the relationship through Councils Or Corporate Elites and Centralized empire.
stages.mechanism: The most defensible position is organized authority with uncertain scale, personnel and coercive structure.
stages.consequence: Achievement is clear; constitutional form is not.
stages.trap: No palace means no state. || Early states can express authority through infrastructure, standards and networks rather than royal monuments.
stages.answer: Polity Debate - Empire, City-States, Councils Or Corporate Elites comprises Polity Debate - Empire, City-States and Councils Or Corporate Elites as its core connected dimensions.

stages.title: RELIGION AND RITUAL - INTERPRETATION WITHOUT BACK-PROJECTION
stages.terms: Religious interpretation should follow the sequence form - context - comparison - alternative - qualified conclusion.
stages.mechanism: Religious interpretation should follow the sequence form - context - comparison - alternative - qualified conclusion.
stages.consequence: Female figurines are abundant at some sites and rare at others, demonstrating regional or functional variation.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: similarity with later Hindu practice proves direct unchanged continuity. || Resemblance may indicate continuity...
stages.answer: Harappan ritual was plural, household and civic; a single standardized creed cannot be reconstructed.

stages.title: GENDER, BURIALS, HEALTH AND THE LIMITS OF SOCIAL RECONSTRUCTION
stages.terms: Burial wealth was generally modest compared with Egyptian or Mesopotamian royal tombs.
stages.mechanism: Burial wealth was generally modest compared with Egyptian or Mesopotamian royal tombs.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that use burial and gender evidence as a lesson in cautious social history, not a...
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: goddess worship means matriarchy. || Divine femininity and ordinary women's authority are separate questions.
stages.answer: Use burial and gender evidence as a lesson in cautious social history, not a route to confident family law.

stages.title: DECLINE AND DEURBANISATION - A MULTI-CAUSAL, REGIONAL PROCESS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Decline And Deurbanisation - A Multi-Causal, Regional Process — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Decline to Deurbanisation - A Multi-Causal, then testing the relationship through Regional Process and Aryan invasion.
stages.mechanism: The mature phase was followed by Late Harappan cultures; people and practices did not vanish.
stages.consequence: Mohenjo-daro and Dholavira show gradual deterioration, while urban life ended more abruptly at Kalibangan and Banawali.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: one flood, one invasion or one drought ended every city. || Different mechanisms operated...
stages.answer: Use "metamorphosis/deurbanisation" with causation, regional variation and continuity.

stages.title: LATE HARAPPAN CONTINUITY, TRANSFORMATION AND SUCCESSOR CULTURES — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Late Harappan levels overlap with Painted Grey Ware at some Punjab-Haryana sites and with Ochre Coloured Pottery in western Uttar Pradesh.
stages.mechanism: Late Harappan levels overlap with Painted Grey Ware at some Punjab-Haryana sites and with Ochre Coloured Pottery in western Uttar Pradesh.
stages.consequence: Overlap shows contact and sequence, not ethnic identity.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: "Continuity" means the entire mature urban system survived unchanged. || Continuity and structural rupture...
stages.answer: Continuity is selective: pottery, crops, craft and population can continue even when cities, script and standardized institutions weaken.

stages.title: RELATIONS WITH NEOLITHIC-CHALCOLITHIC AND VEDIC WORLDS
stages.terms: Technically, Relations With Neolithic-Chalcolithic And Vedic Worlds is analysed by relating Relations With Neolithic-Chalcolithic to Vedic Worlds, then testing the relationship through Earlier farming communities and Contemporary Chalcolithic groups.
stages.mechanism: Migration, admixture and cultural interaction are better models than either violent replacement or timeless ethnic identity.
stages.consequence: Genetics does not directly identify language, religion or self-designation.
stages.trap: aDNA can label an archaeological culture as a modern ethnic or linguistic group. || Genes, language, material culture and political identity are related but non-identical evidence domains.
stages.answer: Relations With Neolithic-Chalcolithic And Vedic Worlds comprises Relations With Neolithic-Chalcolithic, Vedic Worlds and Earlier farming communities as its core connected dimensions.

stages.title: PHASE -> PROCESS -> REGIONAL CHANGE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Phase - Process - Regional Change — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Phase - Process - Regional Change to Mature, then testing the relationship through Late Harappan and It.
stages.mechanism: Use Early, Mature and Late Harappan as a process sequence: regional foundations - integrated urban traits - de-urbanisation and localisation.
stages.consequence: It is not sudden appearance then extinction.
stages.trap: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.answer: Mature urbanism is the core factual phase; Late Harappan continuity prevents a one-line collapse story.

stages.title: SITE-FEATURE TRIADS, NOT A SITE CATALOGUE
stages.terms: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.mechanism: The operative mechanism is that a modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that a modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.answer: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.

stages.title: URBAN WATER AND BUILT FORM — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: They do not securely identify kings, a palace, a granary or one central state.
stages.mechanism: They do not securely identify kings, a palace, a granary or one central state.
stages.consequence: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: they do not securely identify kings, a palace, a granary or one central state.
stages.answer: Grid streets, standard bricks, wells, bathing floors and covered drains securely show planned civic construction and water management.

stages.title: PRODUCTION, MEASUREMENT AND EXCHANGE
stages.terms: No coinage is known; weights and commodities do not tell us the title of a ruler.
stages.mechanism: No coinage is known; weights and commodities do not tell us the title of a ruler.
stages.consequence: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: evidence of coordination - craft/exchange implication - limit on exact political control.
stages.answer: The argument should be: evidence of coordination - craft/exchange implication - limit on exact political control.

stages.title: SCRIPT, RITUAL AND AUTHORITY
stages.terms: Seals, figurines, fire installations, burials and monumental-looking buildings can reveal material practice and repeated symbols; they cannot securely disclose doctrine, named gods, caste or a monarchy.
stages.mechanism: Seals, figurines, fire installations, burials and monumental-looking buildings can reveal material practice and repeated symbols; they cannot securely disclose doctrine, named gods, caste or a monarchy.
stages.consequence: Use 'horned figure', 'female figurines' and 'structure conventionally called...' before advancing a cautious interpretation.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.answer: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.

stages.title: DECLINE AS TRANSFORMATION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.mechanism: A modern archaeological label is not a Harappan self-description.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that river/environmental change, trade disruption and internal reorganisation are contributory explanations, not a settled single...
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: river/environmental change, trade disruption and internal reorganisation are contributory explanations, not a settled single...
stages.answer: River/environmental change, trade disruption and internal reorganisation are contributory explanations, not a settled single cause.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 1: FROM REGIONAL CULTURES TO URBAN INTEGRATION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: The Mature phase shows their unusually wide integration: shared seals, weights, brick conventions and urban features.
stages.mechanism: Shared weights and brick conventions are outcomes of repeated choices and coordination; they are not the initial cause of every town.
stages.consequence: The Late phase is the weakening of this particular urban integration, not the disappearance of every person or practice.
stages.trap: Dholavira's distinctive architecture also demonstrates that integration did not erase regional solutions.
stages.answer: The Mature phase shows their unusually wide integration: shared seals, weights, brick conventions and urban features.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 2: EXTENT, ECOLOGY AND THE URBAN-RURAL SYSTEM — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Ecology creates possibilities and pressures; it does not mechanically determine a political outcome.
stages.mechanism: A coastal or semi-arid site should not be judged by the same expectations as a riverine city.
stages.consequence: Extent is an economic map: river plains, coast and resource zones were connected, not identical.
stages.trap: Cities therefore depended on villages, pastoral areas and resource routes; they were not self-sufficient islands.
stages.answer: Ecology creates possibilities and pressures; it does not mechanically determine a political outcome.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 3: PLANNING, WATER AND EVERYDAY MAINTENANCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Deep Teaching Unit 3: Planning, Water And Everyday Maintenance — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Deep Teaching Unit 3 to Planning, then testing the relationship through Water and Everyday Maintenance.
stages.mechanism: They do not reveal whether a monarch, council, merchant group or several local authorities organised it.
stages.consequence: Calling a raised sector a “citadel” does not prove that it was a royal fort.
stages.trap: The label describes an excavator's interpretation, not a text from the inhabitants.
stages.answer: Town planning means more than a grid seen from above.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 4: THE ECONOMY AS A LINKED SYSTEM — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Deep Teaching Unit 4: The Economy As A Linked System — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Deep Teaching Unit 4 to The Economy As A Linked System, then testing the relationship through A bead and Its.
stages.mechanism: Its raw material had to arrive, specialist labour had to shape it, and finished goods had to move or be exchanged.
stages.consequence: A bead is not just an ornament for a list.
stages.trap: Do not learn crops, beads, weights and trade as disconnected lists.
stages.answer: A Mains paragraph can argue: specialised production and shared metrology indicate an integrated economy, but neither coins nor a named bureaucracy are available to prove a modern market or empire.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 5: EVIDENCE LADDER FOR SCRIPT, POLITY, SOCIETY AND RELIGION
stages.terms: The same object can sit at different levels of the ladder.
stages.mechanism: Use a two-step sentence: “The evidence indicates X because of Y; however, Z remains unresolved because the script is undeciphered and the label is interpretive.” This earns analysis without evasiveness.
stages.consequence: “Undeciphered script” does not license every speculation; it makes the material context more important, not less.
stages.trap: Archaeology does not mean “we know nothing”; it means that the strength of a claim changes with the evidence.
stages.answer: Because the script is undeciphered, they cannot securely name a king, identify a god, translate a law or establish caste.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 6: DE-URBANISATION AS CAUSAL SEQUENCE AND CONTINUITY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: A 20-marker should move from what changed (urban traits, settlement pattern) - possible interacting causes - regional unevenness - continuity.
stages.mechanism: A 20-marker should move from what changed (urban traits, settlement pattern) - possible interacting causes - regional unevenness - continuity.
stages.consequence: It is not a licence to choose one dramatic event.
stages.trap: A river shift or trade change may help explain them, but needs matching chronology and regional context.
stages.answer: Ghaggar-Hakra debates illustrate the rule: many settlements and changing river/environmental conditions matter, but identification with the Vedic Sarasvati and a civilization-wide causal claim are debated.

stages.title: DEEP TEACHING UNIT 7: SITE MEMORY METHOD AND THE FIVE-SENTENCE ANSWER — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: The method works even when one option is partly familiar.
stages.mechanism: In an unfamiliar site question, do not search memory for one glamorous object.
stages.consequence: Add a qualifier when a feature is a conventional function, not a settled fact.
stages.trap: More sites do not necessarily make a better answer.
stages.answer: Memory improves when a site is stored as a triad rather than as an isolated name.
